Ava (Finance Ops): :loudspeaker: Temporary update: effective immediately we are instituting a $5,000/month cap per corporate p-card to reduce exposure after several anomalous vendor charges. This is intended as a short window while Finance completes a vendor activity review; target end date 2026-04-15 unless extended.

Ava (Finance Ops): How this behaves: any charge that would push a card over $5k within a calendar month will be declined at the processor. If you expect legitimate business spend exceeding this, submit the procurement exception form linked below. Exceptions are for critical vendor payments only and require FP&A + Procurement signoff.

Ava (Finance Ops): Links: Confluence FAQ https://redwood.internal/confluence/pcard-temp-cap; Exception form https://redwood.internal/forms/procurement-exception. For customer-impacting vendor payments add "INCIDENT" to the form subject and tag @Sam.

Diego (FP&A): Action for teams: please review vendor commitments and planned card charges for the next 30 days and send reprioritization notes to FP&A by EOD tomorrow. We'll triage exceptions against the updated Q2 forecast.

Lina (Eng Manager): Q: Does this affect pre-approved reserved infra credits or signed Dedicated contracts?

Sam (Procurement): Short answer: no. Pre-approved reserved capacity or existing contractual commitments are grandfathered. The cap applies to new single-card charges only. If autoscaling or burst credits may still generate card charges that exceed the limit, file an exception with the contract reference and cc procurement@redwood.com.

Lina (Eng Manager): Thanks, filing now.

Diego (FP&A): Exceptions will go through a quick cross-functional review (FP&A + Procurement + Finance Ops). Expect a 24-48h turnaround for standard requests; mark "EXPEDITE" for customer-impacting items.

Accounting Bot: Automated note: reconciliation schedule remains unchanged. Please attach receipts in Concur within 5 business days to avoid holds.

Ava (Finance Ops): Apologies for the temporary friction. This helps protect customer funds and company cash while we complete the review. Reach out in-thread or DM me for edge cases. :pray:
